source.title: On the Scalability of Diffusion-based Text-to-Image Generation
source.authors: Hao Li; Yang Zou; Ying Wang; Orchid Majumder; Yusheng Xie; R. Manmatha; Ashwin Swaminathan; Zhuo-Wen Tu; Stefano Ermon; Stefano Soatto

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests analogous scaling functions in text-to-image diffusion models, a different modality and training setting from language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The study fits scaling functions for TIFA text-image alignment, not held-out language-model cross-entropy. It does not test language-model extrapolation, compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, downstream language tasks, or the claimed loss behavior at fixed parameter count. Background citations to language-model scaling laws are not study results.
record.test_reason: The study fits power-law scaling functions for text-to-image diffusion models against compute, parameters and dataset size. This is a new setting with its own result on V5. The fitted quantity is TIFA alignment, a bounded VQA-based score, not held-out loss, and each fit spans roughly one order of magnitude or less. No language-model versions (V1–V4, V6, V7) are tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that T2I diffusion performance improves by properly scaling denoising backbones and training data. Transformer depth is more parameter-efficient than channels, and data quality and diversity matter more than raw size. They fit power-law functions predicting TIFA alignment from compute, model size and dataset size, within a range given sufficient training.
record.recipe_differences: The study fits functions to TIFA scores for image-generation models and image-noun data, rather than measuring held-out language-model cross-entropy over parameters, tokens, and compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that dataset quality affects results: LensArt+SSTK performs better than LensArt-raw despite a similar number of image-noun pairs. It also reports that architecture choices, including transformer depth and channel count, affect alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing transformer depth improves TIFA more per parameter than increasing channels. TD4_4 (1.2B) matches SDXL UNet (2.4B). TIFA at fixed steps correlates slightly better with FLOPs (Spearman 0.936) than with parameters (0.900).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In diffusion text-to-image models, architecture (location and amount of cross-attention, transformer depth) changes alignment substantially at a given parameter count, so parameter count alone poorly predicts performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Dataset quality and caption density matter more than raw dataset size for TIFA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In text-to-image diffusion, data quality and caption enrichment shift the data scaling curve more than dataset size does.

record.problems: The reported scaling fits concern TIFA alignment, not held-out loss. Fits use Pareto-frontier points from the tested diffusion-model variants; uncertainty for the fitted functions is not reported.

untested.parts: Held-out loss (the diffusion training loss) as the scaled quantity; scaling over several orders of magnitude; video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer regimes; extrapolation of the fits to larger runs.
All: no compute-optimal allocation fit. Only a qualitative remark that larger models are more sample-efficient.
All: no comparison of fitting choices.

missing.what: LensArt-raw (1.0B images) vs LensArt (250M) vs LensArt+SSTK at similar image-noun pairs. The filtered 4× smaller set matches TIFA; the raw set sits off the data-scaling curve.
missing.locator: Section 4.2, Fig 7, Fig 11(c), Section 5 'Relationship between performance and data size'

missing.what: Scaling both channels and depth (C384-TD4_12, 4.1B) gives only slightly higher TIFA than SDXL. The authors describe 'a performance limit' to further scaling under TIFA.
missing.locator: Section 3.3, 'Scaling both Channels and Transformer Depth', Fig 4(c)

missing.what: Spearman correlations of TIFA at 600K steps with GFLOPs (0.936) and with parameters (0.900).
PixArt-α transformer variants (0.48B–1.10B) improve with width and depth but stay below the SD2 UNet. They are not included in the power-law fits.

record.verdict_notes: The fits use Pareto-frontier points from a fixed-step training history, are not checked for fit quality or extrapolation, and cover narrow ranges. Labels are hedged accordingly. The authors also say 'larger models are more sample efficient and smaller models are more compute efficient,' echoing Kaplan et al. qualitatively, but this is not quantified and is not treated as a V3 test.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss scaling in parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small language-model runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation for language models.
Loss comparisons at fixed parameter count; the study evaluates image-generation alignment metrics, not loss.
The study tests text-to-image diffusion with TIFA alignment scores. It does not test video, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer, or whether held-out cross-entropy follows the same form.
Downstream language-task performance or its predictability from language-model pretraining loss.
Whether language-model exponents or compute-optimal splits change with fitting choices, or whether language-model curves bend away from a power law.

rows.subject: SDXL variants and SD2 (Pareto-frontier data points)
rows.size_stated: Model variants range from 0.4B to 4.1B parameters.
rows.stage_stated: Diffusion-model training; TIFA measured after training.
rows.operation_detail: Fit a scaling function for TIFA score against total training compute.

conditions.value: fixed-step training history of SDXL variants and SD2

rows.measure: TIFA score S as a function of compute C
rows.note: The authors say the fitted function approximates performance over a range given sufficient training. This is an alignment score, not cross-entropy.
rows.check: A power law S=0.47C^0.02 is fitted to Pareto-frontier points only. Compute spans about 1e11–1e12 GFLOPs, about one order of magnitude. The exponent is tiny, no goodness of fit or uncertainty is given, and the measure is a bounded alignment score, not loss. Baseline is correctly 'not stated'.

rows.subject: SDXL variants and SD2 (Pareto-frontier data points)
rows.size_stated: Model variants range from 0.4B to 4.1B parameters.
rows.stage_stated: Diffusion-model training; TIFA measured after training.
rows.operation_detail: Fit a scaling function for TIFA score against model parameter count.

conditions.value: fixed-step training history of SDXL variants and SD2

rows.measure: TIFA score S as a function of model size N
rows.note: The authors say the fitted function approximates performance over a range given sufficient training. This is an alignment score, not cross-entropy.
rows.check: Pareto-frontier fit S=0.77N^0.11 over 0.4B–4.1B parameters, about one order of magnitude. Separately, Fig 10 reports TIFA at fixed 600K steps, not a parameter-bottleneck-free setting. There is no fit-quality measure, and the measure is a bounded score, not loss.

rows.subject: SDXL variants and SD2 (Pareto-frontier data points)
rows.size_stated: Dataset scale is measured in M image-noun pairs.
rows.stage_stated: Diffusion-model training; TIFA measured after training.
rows.operation_detail: Fit a scaling function for TIFA score against dataset size.

conditions.value: fixed-step training history of SDXL variants and SD2

rows.measure: TIFA score S as a function of dataset size D
rows.note: The authors say the fitted function approximates performance over a range given sufficient training. This is an alignment score, not cross-entropy.
rows.check: Fit S=0.64D^0.03 spans about 1.8B–7.3B image-noun pairs, under one order of magnitude, on SD2 models. The text calls it a 'linear correlation' with cleaned data. LensArt-raw, with similar image-noun pairs to LensArt+SSTK, falls well below the curve, so dataset size alone does not determine the score.

rows.subject: SDXL UNet variants (TD2, TD4, TD12 and TD14)
rows.stage_stated: Training from scratch; TIFA monitored during training.
rows.operation_detail: Vary transformer depth at the 4× downsampling rate.
rows.value: Increasing depth from 2 to 14 continuously improves TIFA score.
rows.locator: Section 3.3, The Effect of Transformer Depth; Figure 4(b)
rows.note: This is an architecture/alignment result, not a fixed-parameter-count comparison of loss.
rows.check: Depth changes alter parameter count (0.9B–3.2B), so this is not a fixed-parameter shape comparison, and the measure is TIFA, not loss. It does not bear on V4 as stated.

relationships.condition: Pareto-frontier SDXL/SD2 UNet variants at 256px on cleaned data, TIFA metric
relationships.reason: Power-law functions of compute, parameters and data fit the frontier points (R1–R3), though over about one order of magnitude with tiny exponents.
relationships.display_finding: Power laws in compute, parameters and data fitted TIFA frontier points over about one order of magnitude, with very small exponents.

relationships.condition: Data-size scaling across datasets of differing quality; off-frontier or combined-scaling models
relationships.reason: Unfiltered LensArt-raw, at similar image-noun pairs, scores well below LensArt+SSTK (R3). Combined channel and depth scaling shows a 'performance limit' under TIFA (text, Fig 4c). The power law is a fitted envelope over a narrow range, without fit statistics.
relationships.display_finding: LensArt-raw underperformed LensArt+SSTK at similar image-noun pairs, while combined channel and depth scaling reached a TIFA performance limit.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
